The epitope, presented in a scaffold of a conserved protein from Pseudomonas aeruginosa with unidentified function, was recognized by mAb HCV1, as measured by ELISA or Octet binding assay. The epitope residues L413, N415, 417NGSW420 and I422 were grafted onto the scaffold, and the flexible N-terminus of the scaffold protein was truncated by four residues. MAb HCV1 also recognized nanoparticles formed from a construct of the epitope-scaffold protein fused to the N-terminus of a ferritin subunit (Asp5) with a 5-aa flexible linker. The fusion protein is capable of assembling into a particle with 24 copies of the epitope scaffold displayed on the surface.

The human mAb specificity was determined by the use of synthetic peptides. While the 12-mer VYLLPRRGPRLG (34-45) gave a low signal, larger peptides such as the epitope were more reactive. The epitope is the shorter peptide tested that was significantly reactive with the mAb. In another experiment, preincubation of hmAb B12.F8 with the epitope inhibits mAb binding to the HCV nucleoprotein in ELISA coated wells.
The epitope-specific mAb reacted with the core protein in ELISA and immunoblot.

The epitope-specific mAb was more reactive with the larger fragment 27-59, suggesting the conformation of the epitope is stabilized in the larger fragment. In another experiment, preincubation of hmAb B12.F8 with the peptide 27-59 inhibits mAb binding to the HCV nucleoprotein in ELISA coated wells just as effectively as the epitope.
The epitope-specific mAb reacted with the HeLa cells transfected with a core protein construct in a immunohistochemistry assay, giving a perinuclear staining not seen in control untransfected cells.

The epitope for the epitope specific mAb was determined by single particle cryo-electron microscopy reconstruction of the quarternary complex of the HCV 1a E1E2 glycoprotein with mAbs AR4A, AT1209, and IGH505 at a resolution of 3.83 Å.

The epitope, presented in a scaffold of the binding domain (E3BD) of human dihydrolipoamide dehydrogenase (E3) binding protein (E3BP), was recognized by mAb IGH526, as measured by ELISA or Octet binding assay. Epitope E1 residues 316HR317, 319AWD321, and 323MM324 were grafted onto the scaffold protein, and a double mutation T16G/F18A was introduced to minimize scaffold-antibody clashes. MAb IGH526 also recognized the epitope inserted into a scaffold of a 50S ribosomal protein (L24E) found in the large ribosomal subunit. MAb IGH526 also recognized nanoparticles formed from a construct of the epitope-scaffold protein fused to the N-terminus of a ferritin subunit (Asp5) with a 5-aa flexible linker. The fusion protein is capable of assembling into a particle with 24 copies of the epitope scaffold displayed on the surface.

The crystal structure of Fab IGH256 in complex with the epitope was determined by molecular replacement. The 11-residue epitope is amidated at the C-terminus.; Unmapped quantitative response: 3D structure 1.75 angstroms

Binding of epitope-specific mAb IGH526 to HCV E1E2 in ELISA was inhibited by peptide NIH 6971. The peptide was also shown to contain the epitope for IGH256 in a pepscan analysis of overlapping peptides spanning the HCV structural proteins core, E1 and E2.
Binding of epitope-specific mAb IGH526 to HCV E1E2 in ELISA was inhibited by peptide H312.

The epitope-specific mAb IGH526 bound to HCV E1E2 antigen expressed in 293T cells in the native state, but did not react to reduced and denatured E1E2, as assayed by ELISA. The authors suggest that IGH256 recognizes a discontinuous epitope on either E1 or E1E2 with a linear epitope spanning E1 (313-327) comprising a major component. Alanine/glycine substitution at residues His316, Trp320 and Met323, at position 3, 7, and 10 in the epitope, respectively, significantly reduced binding. Substitution of Ala319, Met324 and Arg317 also reduced binding.
